turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Hey, good to see you again, just to confirm full name and date of birth.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Haeunwoo Park, November 3rd, 1996.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Thanks, Haeunwoo, it's been what a year and a half, what's going on?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: My eczema's back, bad. It started flaring about three weeks ago, right after I started a new job at Brightline Logistics. The warehouse is freezing and super dry. Where is it this time? Inside, both elbows, behind my knees, my neck, and the backs of my hands are cracking.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: On a scale of zero to ten, how bad is the itch?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Like an eight, it wakes me up at night. My girlfriend Jisoo says I'm scratching in my sleep.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: That's rough, any oozing or yellow crusting.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, nothing like that.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Favors?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Nope.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Any new soaps, detergents, or lotions? No, same stuff, as always.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: What have you been putting on it? I ran out of the triumphs in a loan you gave me last time, so I've been using the drugstore hydrocortisone, the 2 .5 percent. Wait, no, it's the 1 percent. The 2 .5 needs a prescription right.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Right, the 1 percent is the over -the -counter one, and it's just not strong enough for this. Anything else you take.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Cederazine. Ten milligrams every day for my seasonal allergies. Okay,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: and you had asthma as a kid, right? Any breathing trouble now?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, I outgrew that. I haven't used an inhaler since I was like twelve. Good, still no drug allergies. None.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Alright, let's look. In both elbow creases, there are red, scaly, thickened plaques about six by four centimeters each with scratch marks. Same thing behind both knees, a bit smaller. There's patch of dry, red skin on the back of your neck. The backs of both hands are dry with a few small cracks over the knuckles. No weeping and no honey -colored crusting so I don't see signs of infection. Your face and eyelids are clear. I'd estimate about 10 % of your body surface.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yeah, that sounds about right.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: So this is a flare of your atopic dermatitis, probably set off by the cold, dry air at work.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Here's the plan.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I'm restarting Triumcin alone 0 .1 % ointment, twice a day to the patches on your body and hands for two weeks. Then cut back to just weekends, Saturday and Sunday, on the spots that like to come back. Don't use it on your face or groin.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Ointment, not the cream.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Ointment, it's greasier but it works better on dry, cracked skin and it stings less. You can stop the hydrocortisone. For the itch at night, let's add hydroxazine 25 milligrams at bedtime as needed. It'll make you drowsy, so don't drive after taking it. Keep the Cetirizine in the morning.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay. Moisturizing is half the battle.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: A thick fragrance -free cream or plain petroleum jelly at least twice a day and right after a short lukewarm shower. At work, wear cotton -lined gloves when you can.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I can write a note for that. That would help, yes.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: If it keeps flaring even with all this, there are newer options like dupalumab and injection and we can talk about it then. And if you see oozing, yellow crusts, or you get a fever, call us right away. that could be an infection.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Got it. Should I call the same number?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Yes, and we have 555 -0177 for you. Is that still right?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: That's still me. Great.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Let's see you back in four weeks on Monday, November 2nd, and see how the skin's doing.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Sounds good. Thanks, Dr. Haddad.
